items.q: You run OFFSET with distance 5 on a 40 mm diameter circle and click outside the circle. What do you get?
options: A new circle of 30 mm diameter
A new circle of 50 mm diameter
A new circle of 45 mm diameter
A copy of the 40 mm circle moved 5 mm
items.explain: OFFSET moves every point of the circle 5 mm outward, so the radius grows from 20 to 25 and the diameter becomes 50.

items.q: A polar ARRAY of one 8 mm hole with 6 items filling 360 degrees on a 100 mm pitch circle. What is the angle between adjacent holes?
options: 30 degrees
72 degrees
60 degrees
45 degrees
items.explain: Six items spread evenly over a full circle sit 360 / 6 = 60 degrees apart.

items.q: A floor plan is drawn full size in millimetres. You need it printed at 1:100 through a layout viewport. What do you set?
options: SCALE the model objects by 0.01
Plot scale 100:1
Redraw the plan in centimetres
Viewport scale 1:100 (ZOOM 1/100XP)
items.explain: Keep the model at 1:1 and let the viewport do the scaling; 1/100XP means one paper unit shows 100 model units.

items.q: Which statement about turning a layer OFF versus FREEZING it is correct?
options: FROZEN locks editing but keeps the objects visible
OFF deletes the objects; FROZEN only hides them
Both hide the objects; FROZEN also skips them in regeneration and plotting
OFF hides the objects; FROZEN only greys them out
items.explain: Off layers are still processed by the drawing; frozen layers are ignored completely, which is faster and safer for plotting.

items.q: A horizontal line crosses a vertical line. You start TRIM, select the vertical line as the cutting edge, then click the right-hand part of the horizontal line. What happens?
options: Both lines are cut into four pieces
The vertical line is shortened
The right-hand part of the horizontal line is removed
Nothing; TRIM needs a closed boundary
items.explain: TRIM deletes the part of the object you click, up to the cutting edge; the cutting edge itself is untouched.

items.q: You have inserted a block named DOOR 30 times. You edit the block definition and add a handle. What happens to the drawing?
options: All 30 instances update to show the handle
Existing instances stay; only new insertions get the handle
Only the instance you had selected updates
A new block DOOR1 is created
items.explain: Every insertion is a reference to one definition, so changing the definition changes all of them at once.

items.q: The model is in millimetres and the viewport is 1:50. Which setting makes dimension text plot at 3 mm high on paper?
options: Set text height to 0.06
Set DIMSCALE to 1 and dimension in model space
Set DIMSCALE to 0.02
Use annotative dimensions, or set DIMSCALE to 50
items.explain: Text drawn in model space shrinks 50 times through the viewport, so it must be scaled up by 50; annotative styles do this automatically.

items.q: In an electrical single-line diagram of a 415 V distribution panel, a single line runs from the transformer to the incoming MCCB. What does that one line represent?
options: All three phases (and neutral) shown as one line
Only the R phase
The earth conductor
A control cable
items.explain: A single-line diagram shows the power path once per circuit; a small slash with a number, if present, tells how many conductors.

items.q: You start LINE at (0,0) and type @100<30 for the next point. Where does the line end?
items.explain: @100<30 is relative polar entry: 100 units at 30 degrees, so x = 100 cos 30 = 86.6 and y = 100 sin 30 = 50.

items.q: You plot a structural drawing with 'Fit to paper' ticked. Why is this a problem on site?
options: All layers are merged
Lineweights are lost
Only model space is plotted
The printed scale is not a standard scale, so it cannot be read with a scale rule
items.explain: Fit to paper picks whatever scale fills the sheet; site engineers need a stated scale like 1:50 to measure from the print.

items.q: You run FILLET with radius 0 and pick two lines that do not meet. What happens?
options: Error: radius must be greater than zero
Nothing happens
A tangent arc of default radius is added
The lines are extended or trimmed to meet at a sharp corner
items.explain: A zero-radius fillet is the quick way to close a corner: both lines are adjusted until they intersect.
